findings.finding: NASA published a December 2025 Privacy Impact Assessment for Microsoft Copilot confirming NASA licenses Microsoft 365 Copilot (plus the free Copilot Chat / 'M365 Copilot Light') as a digital assistant for government employees and contractors; the PIA discloses no seat count or explicit agency-wide eligibility statement.
findings.exact_quote: Copilot for M365 is a licensed AI-powered tool for use as a digital assistant.
findings.source_title: National Aeronautics and Space Administration Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA): Microsoft Copilot - NASA
findings.notes: VERIFIED against the full PIA via pdftotext extraction. The PIA names the user populations as 'NASA Contractors / Government Employees / Other' but gives NO seat/license count and NO sentence explicitly saying every NASA employee is eligible. It is a licensed (paid) tool, so distribution is bounded by license allocation, not automatically agency-wide; the free Copilot Chat tier is broadly available. Coverage kept 'unknown' (no change) because the public record does not state the eligibility scope. The OMB 2025 inventory reports Microsoft Copilot + Gemini at 1,001-5,000 users against a ~18,000 workforce. Explicit FedScoop and Nextgov searches found only NASA's separate public-facing 'Earth Copilot' science chatbot, not an internal-Copilot rollout story. Most recent source is Dec 2025 (under 6 months old).

findings.finding: ChatGSFC, an internal chat-based AI tool originally built at Goddard Space Flight Center on the open-source LibreChat platform, was scaled to the NASA workforce and is used by over 7,000 people across NASA for tasks from risk analysis to mission planning.
findings.exact_quote: Over 7,000 people across NASA use ChatGSFC to support their work.
findings.source_title: ChatGSFC: Building Composable AI Tools for NASA on Open Source Tooling - Element 84
findings.notes: NEW finding / coverage_assessment OLD pilot -> NEW partial. agent3 framed NASA's Goddard chatbot only as a center-level 'pilot' (FedScoop, Mar 2026). That is true of the Claude-based Goddard pilot, but the picture has since broadened: Element 84 (the contractor that moved ChatGSFC into production under Goddard's Chief AI Officer Matt Dosberg) reports verbatim 'Over 7,000 people across NASA use ChatGSFC to support their work' and states it is available across NASA, not Goddard-only. An AGU 2025 abstract independently describes 'ChatGSFC: Deploying Secure Enterprise AI to Transform Scientific and Engineering Workflows at NASA.' 7,000+ of a ~18,000 workforce is a defined-subset (opt-in, self-service) deployment -> 'partial', not agency-wide 'all'/'most'. The Element 84 page carries no publication date; the AGU25 abstract dates this to late 2025. Treat the 7,000 as a usage figure, not a guaranteed eligibility universe.

findings.tool_name: Center-level Claude chatbots (Goddard pilot, Langley CUI chatbot / inventory name 'ALTIRA')
findings.finding: NASA ran center-specific Claude Sonnet 3.5 chatbots - a Goddard pilot for document editing and code explanation and a Langley chatbot for processing controlled unclassified information; no public source names 'ALTIRA' or gives user counts, and NASA stated in March 2026 it would phase out Anthropic tools to meet a six-month requirement.
findings.exact_quote: a pilot chatbot to assist Goddard Space Flight Center employees with tasks like document editing and explaining code
findings.source_title: NASA chatbots, Treasury coding, OPM drafting: How agencies have deployed Claude - FedScoop
findings.notes: VERIFIED: FedScoop (publication date confirmed 2026-03-04) carries the quote verbatim. coverage kept 'pilot' (no change). These are explicitly center-level pilots, distinct from the broader ChatGSFC tool above. The OMB inventory's internal-tool name 'ALTIRA' (Langley) has no public footprint. FedScoop's March 2026 article adds that NASA spokeswoman Cheryl Warner said the agency 'is evaluating its AI environment and will meet the six-month phase out requirement' - i.e. these Claude-based pilots face decommissioning, reinforcing the 'pilot' (not durable agency-wide) classification. Most recent source Mar 2026.

findings.finding: HUD's September 2025 AI Strategy states that Microsoft Copilot has been deployed to a pilot group of users across HUD; no public source documents an agency-wide rollout or a larger seat count.
findings.exact_quote: Microsoft Copilot has been deployed to a pilot group of users across HUD to help boost efficiency and shift from working on routine, mundane tasks to higher-value work.
findings.source_title: HUD AI Strategy for OMB Memorandum M-25-21 - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
findings.notes: UPGRADE of agent5's HUD finding: agent5 marked HUD Copilot 'pilot' with status 'searched_no_source' and a null exact_quote, relying only on the OMB inventory's 1-100 bucket. QC located an OFFICIAL verbatim source: HUD's own AI Strategy PDF says 'Microsoft Copilot has been deployed to a pilot group of users across HUD' (extracted via pdftotext). coverage_assessment unchanged (pilot -> pilot) but status upgraded searched_no_source -> corroborated, source_type none -> official, confidence low -> high. The word 'pilot' is HUD's own. The HUD M-25-21 Compliance Plan adds that 'HUD currently provides a disclaimer to HUD staff when they attempt to access AI tools' and that HUD 'will be working on broader generative AI guidance' - i.e. broad availability is a future goal, not current state. HUD's other prominent AI items (FHA Virtual Assistant chatbot; DOGE's 'SweetREX' deregulation tool) are task-specific, not general-purpose employee AI. Most recent source Sep 2025 (~8 months old) - may be modestly stale, but it explicitly uses 'pilot' and no newer FedScoop/Nextgov story contradicts it.

findings.finding: NSF's documented Microsoft Copilot use is a pilot confined to the Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP); NSF's own AI policy page lists the use case at the 'Pilot' development stage, not an agency-wide deployment.
findings.exact_quote: Copilot can be used to rewrite and generate text based on user prompts in Microsoft 365 services, including Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, and PowerPoint.
findings.source_title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Strategy - Policies, NSF
findings.notes: CONFIRMED pilot (no change to coverage_assessment). agent4 had it 'pilot' with status searched_no_source and a null exact_quote. QC fetched nsf.gov/policies/ai and confirmed the Copilot use case is explicitly tagged at the 'Pilot' system-development-lifecycle stage ('The use case has been deployed in a limited test or pilot capacity') and is scoped to the TIP directorate. status upgraded searched_no_source -> corroborated, source_type stays official, confidence low -> medium. exact_quote is the verbatim Copilot use-case description from the NSF AI policy page; a stage-specific verbatim sentence ('Pilot') is also present on the page. No NSF-specific seat count exists and no statement that all ~1,700 NSF staff have access. NSF's separate 'AI Builder' summarization use case is 'Deployed' but scoped to the Office of Integrative Activities and is task-specific, not a general-purpose chat assistant. Explicit FedScoop/Nextgov searches surfaced only NSF's external research programs (NAIRR, ExpandAI), not an internal staff AI rollout. The NSF AI policy page is not individually dated; the use cases carry 2025 implementation dates.

findings.finding: NRC launched SimplifAI, an OpenAI-powered internal generative AI chatbot accessed via an internal website, in August 2025; it is NRC's inaugural deployed generative AI use case and adoption is explicitly voluntary, with no public agency-wide seat count.
findings.exact_quote: This isn't something that we are forcing on anyone.
findings.source_title: NRC uses more AI than its inventory suggests - FedScoop
findings.notes: CONFIRMED 'unknown' (no change to coverage_assessment). agent4 had this corroborated and 'unknown'; QC re-verified the FedScoop article. FedScoop quotes an NRC official verbatim that SimplifAI is voluntary ('This isn't something that we are forcing on anyone.') and describes it functioning like commercial chat ('An employee goes to an internal website, enters a query and gets a response'). SimplifAI is NRC's 'inaugural generative AI use case' and one of two AI tools listed as deployed in the inventory. NRC describes a 'metered' / 'small steps' adoption posture. NRC's enterprise AI strategy page (nrc.gov/ai/enterprise-wide-strategy) and FY26 AI Strategic Plan PDF could not be fetched to verbatim (repeated timeouts / HTTP errors) - if a seat count is needed, re-fetch those. No public source states all ~3,000 NRC staff have access; opt-in voluntary use with an unstated install base = 'unknown' under the availability definition. Most recent SimplifAI-specific source is Sep 2025 (~8 months old) - flagged as potentially stale; later NRC coverage (Nextgov Feb 2025; OIG report Dec 2025) does not change the SimplifAI scope picture.

findings.tool_name: Generative AI Assistant / AI Center (OpenAI GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini via Azure)
findings.finding: DOL gave staff access to two OpenAI models (GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini) through Microsoft Azure in April 2025 on an internal platform offering guided applications such as a translator, pros/cons analyzer and memo writer; no public source quantifies coverage.
findings.exact_quote: The two OpenAI models now available to Labor staff are GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini
findings.source_title: OpenAI tech is now available at the Labor Department - FedScoop
findings.notes: CONFIRMED 'unknown' (no change). agent4 had this corroborated and 'unknown'; QC re-verified the FedScoop quote. FedScoop says the models are available to 'Labor staff' but gives no seat count and does not say all ~15,000 DOL employees have access; the deployment is built around specific guided applications rather than an unrestricted enterprise chat rollout, so eligibility scope is genuinely unstated -> 'unknown'. Explicit FedScoop/Nextgov searches found that DOL's headline 2025-2026 AI activity is its external-facing AI Literacy Framework and AI workforce hub (FedScoop, 'Labor Department nears launch of AI workforce hub'; DOL releases Feb-Apr 2026) - those are public/economy-facing programs, NOT internal employee AI tools, and do not change this assessment. Most recent source for the internal tool is Apr 2025 (~13 months old) - flagged as stale; no newer source confirms expansion or contraction.

findings.finding: No DOL-specific public statement was found confirming a department-wide Microsoft Copilot or Copilot Chat rollout or seat count.
findings.notes: CONFIRMED 'unknown' / searched_no_source (no change). QC re-ran explicit FedScoop and Nextgov searches for a DOL Copilot rollout and seat figures; none found. DOL is plausibly covered by the Sept 2025 GSA-Microsoft OneGov deal (free M365 Copilot Chat government-wide) but there is no DOL-specific confirmation. Recorded honestly as no DOL-specific source - not padded.

findings.finding: The OMB 2025 inventory reports 5,001-10,000 SBA users for these commercial tools, but GAO and FedScoop reporting establish that SBA paused essentially all AI use in March 2025 and, as of April 2026, the pause remained in effect except for seven fraud/IT/cyber pilot projects - none a general-purpose chat assistant.
findings.estimated_users: OMB inventory says 5,001-10,000; treated as pre-pause licensing breadth, not an active available deployment
findings.exact_quote: The pause was intended to give the agency time to review use case compliance with new executive orders
findings.source_title: SBA behind the eightball on AI use case reporting, GAO finds - FedScoop
findings.notes: coverage_assessment OLD unknown -> NEW none. agent4 marked SBA 'unknown'. QC re-verified the FedScoop article (publication date confirmed 2026-05-06, the most recent source available) and a corroborating GAO product (GAO-26-107828, May 2026). Both establish that SBA paused ALL AI use in March 2025, that GAO reported all 21 of SBA's 2024 use cases were 'either decommissioned, never deployed, or paused,' and that as of April 2026 the pause REMAINS in effect except for seven pilot/pre-pilot projects in fraud detection, IT operations and cybersecurity. None of those seven are general-purpose chat assistants. Under the corrected availability definition, the question is whether Copilot/Perplexity/Gemini/Grammarly are CURRENTLY available to SBA employees as deployed tools - the verified answer is no: they are paused. Hence 'none', not 'unknown'. The OMB inventory's 5,001-10,000 figure reflects pre-pause licensing breadth (SBA headcount balloons with disaster-relief staff) and is not a current availability count. exact_quote verified verbatim from the fetched FedScoop page.

findings.finding: SSA rolled out the Agency Support Companion, an OpenAI-powered internal generative AI chatbot for employees, announced to staff via internal email in April 2025; access requires completing a four-minute training video, and no public source quantifies how many of SSA's ~57,000-60,000 employees have access.
findings.exact_quote: Staff have to watch a four-minute video with guidelines and best practices to access it.
findings.source_title: SSA is rolling out a new chatbot for employees - Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: CONFIRMED 'unknown' (no change). agent4 had this corroborated and 'unknown'; QC re-verified the Nextgov quote (publication date 2025-04-17). The ASC is a deliberate department-wide offer to employees, announced broadly via internal email, but the four-minute-video gate indicates opt-in provisioning rather than automatic universal access, and no public source gives a take-up or eligibility count -> 'unknown'. NOTE: this is the SSA EMPLOYEE-facing internal chatbot. SSA also runs a separate, much-criticized PUBLIC-facing AI chatbot on its 1-800 phone line (Nextgov, 2025; congressional letters June 2025) - that is a citizen-service tool, NOT a general-purpose employee AI tool, and is intentionally excluded from this finding. Most recent ASC-specific source is Apr 2025 (~13 months old) - flagged as stale; no newer source confirms expansion of the employee tool.
